prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S108: The draft schedule covers payload imaging, recorder management, housekeeping activities, and expected support from the North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna.
S109: For high-volume acquisitions, the schedule also accounts for downlink opportunities through the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna.
S110: The Payload Processing Facility receives planning metadata needed to prepare downstream processing expectations without treating the planning schedule as a commitment to deliver products.
S111: The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are considered during planning only to verify that expected acquisition loads remain compatible with routine processing capacity.
S112: Juniper confirms that planned station use is compatible with network maintenance windows before the schedule is released for command preparation.
S113: The Spacecraft Operations Team uses the Antenna Deicing Notice to assess whether planned support can proceed without adding contingency contact margin.
S114: The Mission Planning System flags conflicts when two activities compete for the same spacecraft resource, ground station resource, or operational staffing interval.
S115: Constraint checking includes slew time, sun-angle limits, power balance, thermal recovery time, recorder capacity, command load size, and required separation between incompatible activities.
S116: The Flight Dynamics Team reviews cases where orbital uncertainty or contact geometry could reduce the execution margin for a planned acquisition or downlink.
S117: The Payload Calibration Team reviews planned calibration activities when they share resources with revenue observations or affect instrument configuration states.
S118: After schedule convergence, the Mission Planning System exports a command preparation package to the command engineering workflow at the Mission Control Center.
S119: The Command Validation Gateway, also called Osprey in this section, performs independent validation of command stacks before they are eligible for operational approval.
S120: Command stack validation checks syntax, timing, parameter ranges, sequencing rules, spacecraft mode compatibility, and consistency with the approved schedule baseline.
S121: The Command Validation Gateway rejects command stacks that contain unapproved manual edits, missing provenance, expired configuration references, or activities outside the planning authority window.
S122: The Telemetry Ingest Service is consulted for the latest spacecraft state needed to confirm that the command assumptions still match actual configuration and health.
S123: The Orbit Determination Engine provides the current orbital solution used to confirm time-tagged events, contact visibility, and any attitude-dependent observation geometry.
S124: The Product Quality Service may add planning feedback when previous acquisitions indicate that a requested geometry or instrument mode is unlikely to meet quality objectives.
